theory.title: Gerundios e infinitivos
theory.explanation: Algunos verbos van seguidos de gerundio (-ing), como enjoy, avoid, suggest y finish; otros suelen llevar infinitivo con to, como decide, hope, plan y manage. Después de una preposición utiliza gerundio. Algunos verbos cambian de significado según lleven gerundio o infinitivo: remember doing describe recordar una experiencia pasada; remember to do significa no olvidar una tarea. Stop doing es dejar una actividad; stop to do es detenerse para hacer otra cosa. Utiliza infinitivo de propósito para explicar por qué haces algo.
theory.tip: Fíjate en la función de cada estructura y en el contexto antes de elegir la forma verbal.

patterns.label: Enjoy + -ing: disfrutar haciendo algo
examples:
I enjoy learning languages.
→ Disfruto pasando tiempo al aire libre.

patterns.label: Avoid + -ing: evitar hacer algo
examples:
She avoids spending money unnecessarily.
→ Ella decidió cambiar su rutina diaria.

patterns.label: Suggest + -ing: sugerir hacer algo
patterns.pattern: He suggested taking a short break.
examples:
He suggested taking a short break.
→ Deberíamos evitar tomar decisiones precipitadas.

patterns.label: Finish + -ing: terminar de hacer algo
examples:
They finished decorating the room.
→ Él sugirió quedar más temprano.

patterns.label: Decide + to: decidir hacer algo
patterns.pattern: We decided to move closer to work.
examples:
We decided to move closer to work.
→ Tengo muchas ganas de empezar mi nuevo curso.

patterns.label: Hope/plan + to: esperar/planear hacer algo
patterns.pattern: I hope to study abroad next year.
examples:
I hope to study abroad next year.
→ Consiguieron terminar el proyecto a tiempo.

patterns.label: Manage + to: conseguir hacer algo
patterns.pattern: She managed to save enough money.
examples:
She managed to save enough money.
→ Me apunté al club para hacer nuevos amigos.

patterns.label: Adjetivo + infinitivo
examples:
It was difficult to choose.
→ Recuerda traer tu cuaderno.

patterns.label: Preposición + -ing
patterns.pattern: He's interested in working with children.
examples:
He's interested in working with children.
→ Recuerdo haber visitado ese lugar de niño/a.

patterns.label: Infinitivo de finalidad
patterns.pattern: I joined the course to improve my English.
examples:
I joined the course to improve my English.
→ Vale la pena esforzarse cuando algo importa.

content.passage: For years, Daniel wanted to learn to play the guitar, but he kept putting it off. He enjoyed listening to music and often imagined performing with friends. One day, his colleague suggested joining a beginner's class. Daniel decided to give it a try, although he was worried about making mistakes. At first, he found it difficult to practise regularly. He managed to create a short evening routine and avoided checking his phone during practice. His teacher recommended playing for fifteen minutes every day rather than trying to learn everything at once. Daniel also remembered to bring his notebook to each lesson. After three months, he could play several songs and felt more confident. He realised that making progress required patience and that small habits could lead to important changes. Now he is looking forward to performing at a local event.

items.prompt: Describe a new activity you decided to try.
items.modelAnswer: I decided to take up swimming last year because I wanted to become fitter. At first I found it difficult, but I managed to practise twice a week and now I really enjoy going to the pool.

items.prompt: Talk about a habit you would like to change.
items.modelAnswer: I'd like to avoid checking my phone first thing in the morning. I plan to leave it in another room and spend a few minutes reading instead.

items.prompt: Describe a difficult decision you had to make.
items.modelAnswer: I had to decide whether to accept a new job. I considered the benefits and drawbacks, spoke to my family and finally chose the opportunity that offered more learning.

items.prompt: Explain how you keep motivated when learning something.
items.modelAnswer: I try to set small goals and remember why I started. I enjoy seeing progress, and I avoid comparing myself with other learners.

items.prompt: Talk about something you enjoy doing in your free time.
items.modelAnswer: I enjoy cooking because it helps me relax and try new ideas. I also like inviting friends over to share the food.

items.prompt: Describe advice you would give someone who wants to build a good habit.
items.modelAnswer: I'd recommend starting with a small action and doing it regularly. It's important to avoid expecting immediate results and to keep trying.

items.prompt: Talk about a time you managed to achieve a goal.
items.modelAnswer: I managed to complete a long-distance walk after training for several months. I had to plan my routine carefully and remember to rest.

items.prompt: Describe something you stopped doing and why.
items.modelAnswer: I stopped drinking coffee late in the evening because it affected my sleep. I replaced it with herbal tea and now I sleep better.

items.prompt: Explain the difference between remember doing and remember to do.
items.modelAnswer: Remember doing means you have a memory of an action in the past. Remember to do means you must not forget a task you need to complete.

items.prompt: Talk about a decision that created a good opportunity.
items.modelAnswer: I decided to volunteer at a community centre. I wanted to meet people and improve my communication skills, and it became a valuable experience.

content.audioTranscript: Mia: Have you made a decision about the evening course? Josh: Yes. I decided to enrol because I want to improve my writing. Mia: Do you enjoy studying after work? Josh: I do, but I need to avoid staying up too late. Mia: Have you considered taking the Saturday class? Josh: I did. The teacher suggested joining the online group first. Mia: That sounds useful. Josh: Yes, and I managed to speak to a former student. She recommended practising a little every day. Mia: Are you looking forward to it? Josh: Definitely. I hope to meet new people, and I plan to keep a learning diary. Mia: Remember to check the start date. Josh: Thanks. I'll write it down now.
